subject: Family Business Management
text: Read the case and answer the following. The Raman family owns and operates “Raman Textiles,” a third-generation family business specializing in textile manufacturing. Founded by Mr. Vijay Raman in 1970, the company is currently managed by his two sons, Arjun and Rohit. The third generation, consisting of four grandchildren aged between 25 and 35, is preparing to take on roles in the business. Despite steady business growth, the family is experiencing several internal challenges. Arjun and Rohit disagree about who from the next generation should assume leadership roles. One grandchild, Nisha, has demonstrated strong managerial ability, but her role remains uncertain as some family members prefer seniority-based involvement rather than merit-based selection. Disagreements have also emerged regarding ownership distribution among third-generation members, particularly because some are actively involved in the business while others are not. Family discussions about these matters often become emotional and unstructured, resulting in unresolved conflicts and growing tension among family members. As the business continues to expand and more family members become involved, the Raman family is finding it increasingly difficult to coordinate expectations, responsibilities, and decisions affecting both the family and the business.
